evals.prompt: Please check this end-to-end test flow file for quality problems. Use the orchestration-quality-control skill with profile: aplicatudo-e2e. Ask me any missing choices with the usual question screen. Only use the skill rules and this file. Write a short plain report. Ask me before changing any file.
evals.expected_output: Asks which language to use for the report if needed. Reads only the skill rules and the given file. Finds that login values sit inside the flow instead of a data file. Suggests moving them. Asks before editing.

assertions.text: Produces a short plain-language report with what is wrong, which rule, where, and what to change
Flags login or environment values living inside the flow instead of a data file
Does not edit the target file before an explicit apply confirmation
Does not open unrelated project files for the quality check
Reader-facing text avoids abbreviations, acronyms, and decorative symbols

evals.prompt: Please check this domain description file for quality problems. Use the orchestration-quality-control skill with profile: aplicatudo-e2e. Write the report in English. Do not change the file until I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Uses English. Finds that the domain file mixes business rules with passwords, screen ids, wait times, and database field notes. Suggests splitting those out. Does not edit until the user agrees.

assertions.text: Produces a short plain-language English report
Flags mixing of business rules with passwords, screen ids, wait times, or database field notes
Does not edit the file before user approval
Names broken rules in plain words rather than internal codes
Stays isolated to packaged rules plus the selected file

evals.prompt: Please check this whole folder of end-to-end test files for quality problems. Use the orchestration-quality-control skill with profile: aplicatudo-e2e. Look for helper flows that nothing calls, and for screen ids that collide when only the first nineteen characters are compared. Stay inside this folder.
evals.expected_output: Checks only files in the folder. Finds an unused helper flow and/or colliding screen ids. Writes a short plain report. Asks before editing.

assertions.text: Treats the folder as the target set and does not open files outside it
Flags an unused helper flow and/or colliding screen ids within the folder
Produces a short plain-language report
Asks before applying edits
Avoids abbreviations and acronyms in the reader-facing report

evals.prompt: Please check this rules file for quality problems. Use the orchestration-quality-control skill with profile: aplicatudo-e2e. Write the report in English. Only use the skill rules and this file. Ask me before changing any file.
evals.expected_output: Treats the file as a rules generator source. Flags rationale clauses (because / so that / which allows) and first/then sequencing as rule-authoring problems. May also note generator gaps or contradictions against the profile's packaged artifact rules. Does not edit until the user agrees. Stays isolated.

assertions.text: Treats the target as a rules file / generator source
Flags rationale clauses or first/then sequencing as rule-authoring form problems
Produces a short plain-language English report
Does not edit the file before user approval
Stays isolated to packaged rules plus the selected file
